critical_code_review_comments: career_score.py:_activite uses regularity=min(n,10)/10 (saturates at 10) and penalty -0.4*poor ratio — correctly stops rewarding sheer volume. The volume-vs-quality invariant holds in unit test (good 20 priority-A/B with 5 interviews > poor 200 priority-C).
career_score.py:_ips_moyen falls back to all apps with ips if no 'applied' ones exist — reasonable default.

router.py:next_application_code uses find_one_and_update $inc + upsert with ReturnDocument.AFTER on counters collection keyed by year — atomic, race-safe, yearly reset. Unique index on applications.code enforces uniqueness.

router.py:_run_pack writes every part+ips+decision_report into application_versions collection AND mirrors into applications (fast reads) — storage doubled but intentional to keep each version immutable. ips_history appended via $push on applications.
router.py:reanalyze returns 409 when current status is 'generating' — guards concurrent reanalyses. Good.
router.py:_recover_interrupted marks any version left as 'generating' at startup as error 'Génération interrompue' — correct for hot-reload scenarios (as noted in agent context about v2 of seed app).
compare.py: deterministic diff by criterion key with points delta; input_changes extend to profile_snapshot (certifications/skills/goals adds) — covers Career Memory evolution.
decision_report.py: builds from IPS rows deterministically (strengths = top-3 ≥7, weaknesses = bottom-3 <6) and merges AI-provided improvement_actions when available — never empty by construction.

models.py EntityPatch uses `changes: dict` which bypasses per-field validation on PATCH. Non-blocking: router.py update_entity passes `{...cur, **changes}` through the full model_dump — invalid Literal values would still raise 422 via pydantic. OK.
router.py:DELETE sets archived:true + archived_at + timeline entry; _own filters archived:{$ne:true} so archived apps return 404 on GET as required. Versions remain in application_versions. OK.
PackView.jsx passes `${a.code} · v${shownVersion}` as PackRef; DocTools splits on space and uses `${code}_${name}` for file names — all PDF/DOCX downloads start with CO-… as spec'd.
